SMTO-UI-0062 — Sign-in was not accepted

GUID: 58b26b1b-00d1-5b1c-8eed-22db9db03873
Slug: portal-login-rejected
Domain: UI · Subsystem: authentication

What happened

  • SMTO didn't accept that username and password together. For security it doesn't say which part was wrong, and a disabled account shows the same message.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Type your username and password again. Make sure Caps Lock is off and that your password manager filled in the account for this SMTO server. Passwords must match exactly, including capital letters.
  2. If you're still refused, ask your administrator to check that your account is enabled and, if needed, reset your password on the Users page. A disabled account and a wrong password look the same here, and only an administrator can tell which it is.
  3. After a few failed tries, wait a full minute before trying again. SMTO pauses sign-in for about a minute after repeated failed attempts to protect your account.

What success looks like

  • Your workspace opens under the right account.

If it still fails

  • Ask your administrator for a temporary password, then choose a new one when SMTO asks. Never send your password in an error report, chat or email, and never include browser cookies.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • POST /auth/login returned 401 because the account store raised LoginDenied: the username and password did not match an enabled account that isn't being deleted (or the sign-in request was malformed).

What this means

  • The supplied username and password did not establish a session. This reports access to the current request, not the outcome of previous operations.

Why this can happen

  • The supplied username and password did not establish a session.

How to diagnose it

  • Your workspace opens under the intended account.

How to fix it

  • Login returns the same 401 for a wrong password, an unknown username, a disabled or deleting account, or a password changed during sign-in; usernames match case-insensitively but passwords are exact. An administrator can check the account's Status on the Users page (/user) and use Reset password to issue a temporary password.
  • Check the username and password and enter them again. If you no longer know the password, ask an administrator to reset it.

Retry and execution caution

  • Your workspace opens under the intended account.

How to verify the fix

  • Your workspace opens under the intended account.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained task data or repeat an operation with an unknown outcome.

Technical notes

  • Authentication guidance never changes account permissions or replays task work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
